questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the time complexity of an algorithm that takes a constant amount of time to execute, regardless of input size?
questions.solution: The correct answer is O(1) because the algorithm's execution time does not depend on the input size. Constant time complexity means the number of operations remains the same for any input size.
questions.explanation: In big O notation, O(1) represents constant time complexity, O(n) represents linear time complexity, O(n^2) represents quadratic time complexity, and O(log n) represents logarithmic time complexity.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to choose O(n) or O(n^2), assuming that the algorithm's time complexity increases with input size. However, since the execution time remains constant, regardless of input size, the correct answer is O(1).

questions.stem: What is the big O notation for an algorithm whose running time grows linearly with the input size?
questions.solution: The correct answer is O(n) because the algorithm's running time increases linearly with the input size. Each additional element in the input contributes one more operation to the execution.
questions.explanation: In big O notation, O(1) represents constant time complexity, O(n) represents linear time complexity, O(n^2) represents quadratic time complexity, and O(log n) represents logarithmic time complexity.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to choose O(n^2), which indicates a quadratic growth rate. However, since the running time grows in direct proportion to the input size, the correct answer is O(n).

questions.stem: What does big O notation help us determine about an algorithm?

choices.A: The exact number of operations performed by the algorithm.
choices.B: The minimum amount of memory required for the algorithm to run.
choices.C: The upper bound on the growth rate of the algorithm's running time with respect to input size.
choices.D: The average- case performance of the algorithm.

questions.solution: Big O notation helps us determine the upper bound on the growth rate of an algorithm's running time as the input size increases. It provides a way to compare and analyze algorithms based on their scalability.
questions.explanation: Big O notation does not provide exact operation counts, memory requirements, or average-case performance; it focuses on worst-case scenario analysis for estimating how an algorithm's efficiency scales with larger inputs.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to choose A, which would require a more detailed analysis of the algorithm. Big O notation deals with scalability and growth rates rather than exact operation counts or memory usage.

questions.stem: An algorithm has a time complexity of O(n log n). Which of the following statements best describes its performance?

choices.A: Its running time grows linearly with the input size.
choices.B: Its running time grows quadratically with the input size.
choices.C: Its running time grows faster than linear but slower than quadratic with the input size.
choices.D: Its running time grows exponentially with the input size.

questions.solution: The time complexity of O(n log n) means that the algorithm's running time grows faster than linear (O(n)) but slower than quadratic (O(n^2)). It is an intermediate growth rate between linear and quadratic.
questions.explanation: In big O notation, O(n log n) represents an algorithm whose running time increases at a rate proportional to the input size multiplied by its logarithm. This is faster than linear but slower than quadratic growth.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to choose A or B, which represent simpler growth rates. The presence of 'log n' in the complexity indicates a more complex relationship between running time and input size.

questions.stem: What does it mean when an algorithm has a big O notation of O(1) for both its worst-case and average-case performance?

choices.A: The algorithm always takes the same amount of time to execute, regardless of input size.
choices.B: The algorithm's running time is highly dependent on the specific input data.
choices.C: The algorithm has a linear time complexity in all cases.
choices.D: The algorithm's running time grows quadratically with the input size.

questions.solution: When an algorithm has a big O notation of O(1) for both its worst-case and average-case performance, it means that the algorithm always takes the same amount of time to execute, regardless of input size. The running time is constant.
questions.explanation: In big O notation, O(1) represents constant time complexity, meaning the number of operations remains the same for any input size. This applies to both worst-case and average-case scenarios.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to choose B or C, which suggest that the running time depends on input data or grows linearly with the input size. However, O(1) indicates constant time complexity, independent of input size.

questions.stem: Which big O notation best describes an algorithm whose running time is proportional to the square root of the input size?
questions.solution: The correct answer is O(sqrt(n)), as it indicates that the algorithm's running time grows in proportion to the square root of the input size.
questions.explanation: In big O notation, O(sqrt(n)) represents an algorithm whose running time increases with the square root of the input size. This growth rate is slower than linear (O(n)) but faster than logarithmic (O(log n)).
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to choose A, which represents quadratic time complexity. However, since the running time grows with the square root of the input size, not the size itself, the correct answer is O(sqrt(n)).

questions.stem: What does it mean when an algorithm has a big O notation of O(n^2) for its best-case performance?

choices.A: The algorithm always takes quadratic time to execute.
choices.B: The algorithm's running time is never better than quadratic, regardless of input size.
choices.C: There exists at least one input case where the algorithm performs quadratically.
choices.D: The algorithm has a constant time complexity in all cases.

questions.solution: When an algorithm has a big O notation of O(n^2) for its best-case performance, it means that there exists at least one input case where the algorithm's running time grows quadratically with respect to the input size.
questions.explanation: In big O notation, O(n^2) represents quadratic time complexity. The fact that it is mentioned as the best-case performance indicates that there are scenarios where the algorithm performs worse than this, but at least one case exists where it reaches quadratic growth.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to choose A or B, which suggest that the running time is always quadratic or never better. The correct answer highlights that there is at least one input scenario where the performance is quadratic, not necessarily all scenarios.
